sections.h2: Where Polk County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds in the Polk County courthouse complex at 40 Courthouse St., Columbus, NC 28722. Postal mail uses PO Box 308. Weekday hours are 8:30 to 5:00, and the phone is (828) 894-8450.

The office files deeds, powers of attorney, cancellations of deeds of trust and plats. It also keeps marriage, birth and death records, issues marriage licenses by appointment only, and handles assumed business name certificates. A home sale reaches this counter at the very end, once the deed is signed.

sections.h2: How a recorded deed reaches the tax records
sections.html:
The county updates its tax records after a deed is recorded. A recorded plat also prompts an update, with the tax side working alongside the GIS department on mapping.

Sellers often miss the January 1 rule. Polk County treats whoever held title on that date as the taxpayer for the year, even if the house sells in March. Splitting the bill with a buyer is a private agreement, so take that question to the closing attorney or the agent. Give the tax office a correct mailing address so notices find the right person.

sections.h2: When the GIS map still shows the old owner
sections.html:
Give it time. Parcel data refreshes every one to two months, so a name can lag behind a fresh deed.

  • Recording comes first, and the map follows.
  • If a sale closed in the last two months, wait before worrying.
  • Past two months, call the tax office at (828) 894-8954.
  • For general ownership and transfer questions, call (828) 894-8500.

Write down the book and page of your recorded deed. The tax office may want it if a name needs correcting.

One fee schedule applies to every register of deeds in the state, printed in G.S. 161-10. Phone Columbus for the final amount before mailing anything. The statute's figures are below.

Statewide recording fees as they apply in Polk County
DocumentFee
General instrument such as a deed$26.00 to start, $4.00 per page past page 15
Home loan security instrument$64.00 to start, $4.00 per page past page 35
Lender's release of a loanNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 per further page

The office collects fees before it files anything. A non-standard document adds $25.00, and each extra instrument in one packet adds $10.00.

The seller pays. The rate is a dollar for each $500 of price or value, rounding any remainder up (see the excise tax statute). It is handed over before the deed gets recorded.

Polk County and the State split the money in equal halves. Check the excise tax line on your settlement statement against the sale price.

sections.h2: Why record a Polk County deed right away
sections.html:
The state recording statute ranks competing claims by who registered first. Until the paper is on file in Columbus, an unrecorded deed or option offers no protection against lien creditors or purchasers who paid value.

Two practical points follow. A deed from an earlier family transfer that never reached the office should be recorded before the house is sold. And a paid-off loan clears title only when the lender files its release. The county's Property Check sign-up emails an alert if anything new is filed against your name, which suits a house nobody lives in.

Chapter 47H governs seller-financed deals on homes of up to four families. Within five business days the seller must file the contract itself or a brief memorandum describing it. The buyer may back out until midnight on the third business day.

If either side of a Polk County deal works this way, record promptly and have an attorney read the papers. A forfeiture needs a written notice that gives at least 30 days to cure.

sections.h2: Who else touches a Polk County home sale?
sections.html:
Beyond the register, a sale usually involves the county tax office, which values the parcel and prints the bill, and the settlement agent, who runs the title search and the closing. The register's office coordinates with the tax department, the health department, inspections and the court.

A house tied up in probate or foreclosure goes through the court clerk first. The deed that finally transfers the land still comes back to the Columbus office to be recorded.

sections.h2: Other services at the Polk County register's office
sections.html:
Marriage licenses are by appointment only. Applicants complete a form online and bring it to the appointment, scheduled by phone at (828) 894-8450 or by email.

  • Vital records: births, deaths and marriages recorded in Polk County can be bought online. Records from elsewhere cannot.
  • Assumed business names: owners must refile at the local register's office to stay on the statewide registry.
  • Property Check: a sign-up that warns you about new filings under your name.
  • Powers of attorney: the register records them along with deeds.

A seller who runs a small business from the house or who holds a recorded power of attorney for a parent should ask about these items before closing, so the paperwork lines up with the deed.

sections.h2: What to bring or send to the Columbus office
sections.html:
Phone first at (828) 894-8450 to confirm payment and mail-in details. Then gather the items below so the clerk has everything in one visit.

  • The signed deed, or the plat if you are splitting a parcel.
  • Payment for the excise tax, plus the recording fee quoted by the office.
  • The parcel number printed on your last tax bill.
  • The buyer's mailing address, so later notices arrive.

A month or two after recording, check the parcel on the county GIS site. A plat is the one paper that also reshapes the map, since the tax office and GIS department work together to update mapping after a plat is filed.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
Get the current balance from the Polk County tax office, then tell the closing attorney who owes that year's bill. Tax is due September 1 and can be paid at face value through January 5 (see the collection statute).

A direct cash purchase can shorten the timeline for an inherited, vacant, rented or run-down house. The recording work described above stays the same either way: the signed deed, the excise tax and the filing fee still go through the Columbus counter, and the buyer or the closing office usually handles the trip.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
The path is short but the order matters. First, the closing office collects the excise tax and the recording fee. Second, the signed and notarized deed goes to the Columbus counter, where it receives a time stamp. Third, the tax office updates its records, and the GIS parcel map follows within a month or two. Fourth, you or your attorney keep the book and page number for your files.

If anything is missing, such as a payment or a page, the clerk cannot file the deed, and the time stamp slips. For that reason many closings send the packet the same day the funds are released.

faqs.q: What hours does the Polk County Register of Deeds keep?
faqs.a: The Columbus office at 40 Courthouse St. is open weekdays, 8:30 to 5:00. Phone (828) 894-8450 to confirm, especially around holidays.

faqs.q: If I sell in spring, who owes that year's Polk County tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner carries the liability. Whether the buyer reimburses you is settled privately at closing.

faqs.q: How big is the state's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: A dollar for each $500 of price or value. The selling side pays it at the register's counter.

faqs.q: Can I buy Polk County birth and death records online?
faqs.a: Yes, with one limit. Only vital records recorded in Polk County can be bought online, so a certificate from another county must be requested there.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a loan release in Polk County?
faqs.a: No. A lender's release of a loan carries no fee. The lender is the one that files it, so ask yours to do so at payoff.
